newsitem.title: USA: Dow index edges shyly to record high.
newsitem.headline: Dow index edges shyly to record high.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average racked up its second record close in a row Tuesday, though the rally was far more subdued than Monday's 143-point gain.
The Dow rose 10.83 points to 7,225.32, surpassing the previous day's record of 7,214.49, and setting its 17th high for the year.
Analysts said the market was caught in cross-currents as some investors rushed back into stocks, while others cashed in profits from the recent surge.
Despite the record finish, stocks clearly lacked the sizzle that sent a bevy of Wall Street records toppling just a day ago.
"The action today was indicative of the market's split personality," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
"The technical condition of the market remains outstanding and the breadth has been impressive in recent sessions," Crane said. "But then on the other hand, we've come a long way."
Market breadth was neutral, with advancing issues and declines running in a near dead heat, as 1,260 stocks rose while 1,266 fell.
But the modest rise in the Dow masked a frenzied day in terms of volume. On the New York Stock Exchange, volume topped 601 million shares for only the seventh time in history.

Analysts said the brisk recovery in stocks after the plunge of 700 points in the Dow index between March 12 and April 11, had rekindled interest among investors eager to hop back on an apparently resurgent bull market.
But they also cautioned that near-term gains were likely to be limited at these again lofty levels.

"I do feel the bulk of the near-term gains are probably already in the market, and that's looking both technically and rationally," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
Still, Barthel said the momentum of the rally, which has lifted several indexes such as the Standard & Poor's and NYSE Composite to new highs, may foreshadow more gains.
"We'll probably get a period of consolidation, but rallies don't usually end in a one-time burst like this," he said. "I'm certainly very optimistic."
Several factors should hold the market in check for the next couple of weeks, most importantly the approaching May 20 meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting group.

Wall Street is more divided on whether that meeting will result in a second interest rate hike than they were heading into the Fed's March meeting, something that some analysts say could pose troubles.
"Everybody in March knew they were going to raise rates and it still caused a considerable amount of indigestion when they did," Crane said.
This time around, he said, the market may not be as ready to accept another monetary tightening.
Technology stocks ended broadly lower, hit by profit-taking and dragged down by a weak showing from bellwether chip maker Intel Corp.
Intel slid 4-1/2 to 158 on concerns about a possible bug in its high-end Pentium II and Pentium Pro processers. Several investment firms also downgraded the shares.
Internet sevice provider BBN Corp. jumped 6-1/4 to 28-7/8 after accepting a $29 per share acquisition offer from telephone company GTE Corp.
GTE, which also announced it now expects 1997 earnings per share growth to be slightly positive at best instead of the double-digit growth it earlier forecast, fell 2-3/8 to 45.
BTG Inc. tumbled 5-7/16 to 9-13/16. Late Monday, the company reported a quarterly loss and said it had fallen out of compliance on lending covenants, for which it was seeking waivers.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 10.94 points to 1,328.30.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 2.48 points to 827.76. The American Stock Exchange index was off 2.07 to 570.51.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.66 to 430.77. The average share was down 6 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,800.262 down 17.04 or 0.22 percent.
